newsitem.title: ROMANIA: World Bank chief discusses loans with Romania.
newsitem.headline: World Bank chief discusses loans with Romania.

text.p: World Bank President James Wolfensohn met Romania's new centrist leaders on Monday and the government suggested the Bank would provide additional sums under its programme of agreed credits for the Balkan country.
A government statement said the Bank would be increasing credits for this year to about $600 million.

"The amounts granted to Romania are greater than originally planned," Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea told reporters after an initial round of talks. "We think the World Bank will support our reform programme over the next three years."
But an official from the Bank's Bucharest office said discussions on the package of credits were still under way and no final decision had been taken.
"The figure may end up higher or lower. We cannot say for the time being," the official said.

The government statement said Wolfensohn praised the reforms introduced in February, within weeks of the centrists' ousting ex-communists in general elections. It quoted him as saying that the Bank would support Bucharest's plans to cushion reforms by increasing child benefit and other related measures.
Wolfensohn, making the first visit to Romania in 20 years by a World Bank president, was to brief reporters later in the day after meeting President Emil Constantinescu.

Resident World Bank representative Francois Ettori said last week that $300 million in credits had been agreed for this year for reforming agriculture and helping underpin the government's social policies.
Discussions were also under way for resuming disbursement of a $180 million loan for restructuring enterprises. All credits are to be approved by the Bank's board next month.
Late last month, the International Monetary Fund approved $430 million in credits for Romania.
Both the World Bank and IMF suspended credits last year after complaining that the leftist government then in power had overshot spending targets.
